examples.title: Sine and key signals
examples.play: Play one note, then a chord. This minimal gate has no release tail.

examples.title: Units, pitch and gain
examples.play: Any key opens the same 440 Hz pair. Change 440hz slightly to hear beating.

examples.title: Signal arithmetic
examples.play: Hold a note, then release it. Use overlapping notes to hear voice behavior.

examples.title: Poly and ADSR release
examples.play: Hold two notes. Release one while keeping the other held; only its own envelope releases.

examples.title: Mono, legato and glide
examples.play: Hold a low note, press a higher note, then release the higher note first. Pitch glides back.

examples.title: Mono retrigger
examples.play: Overlap two keys, then change zero to current and compare the attack from a nonzero envelope level.

examples.title: Filter envelope
examples.play: Hold a note and hear the tone darken. Change lowpass to highpass in the dropdown.

examples.title: LFO in hertz
examples.play: Hold one note. Observe p_motion using a Voice capture. Free phase, delay and fade initialize from engine time; they do not restart on each key.

examples.title: Tempo and LFO trigger
examples.play: Change shape and mode using their dropdowns. Trigger enables retrigger/one_shot; sync enables transport.

examples.title: Unison and stereo spread
examples.play: Use headphones. Compare spread 0 and 0.85, then inspect width_power. Spread changes pan positions, not detune.

examples.title: Distortion modes
examples.play: Hold one note and switch softclip, hardclip and fold. Watch added harmonics; match level before judging preference.

examples.title: Stereo routing
examples.play: Change both 0.3 values together to 1. Mid/side reconstruction then recovers the original stereo signal.

examples.title: Probe before and after a filter
examples.play: Hold C3. Inspect and listen to raw and filtered, then drag cutoff. Keep both observations on the same capture selection.

examples.title: Compare waveform, spectrum and power
examples.play: Release the key, switch files, then replay C3 at the same velocity and hold it. Inspect diff, spectrum_diff and power_diff in turn; they answer different questions.

examples.title: Control probes and analysis arithmetic
examples.play: Choose the sounding Voice for p_amp. Inspect power_percent for the audio power ratio, not a loudness score.

examples.title: Class knob metadata
examples.play: Drag cutoff in code or Signal Flow. Its range and default come from the class. Double-click the knob to reset.

examples.title: Typed class composition
examples.play: The class packages a signal graph. Each make gets its own filter state; this is not a reference to another instrument.

examples.title: Pure if and note ranges
examples.play: Play below and above C3. The lower range blends back part of the waveform difference.

examples.title: Stereo motion instrument
examples.play: Play a sustained note or chord. Change LFO shape, distortion mode and spread. Inspect color_diff or width_power separately. Keep capture on Mid for width_power, since width = side(shaped) already extracts Side; Side projection is useful for the stereo p_after.

examples.title: Rolling bass: mid and sub
examples.play: Use the built-in 138 BPM bass sequence or short MIDI notes. The program makes mid and sub layers; it does not generate a kick.

examples.title: Developer mode: waveform formula
examples.play: Hold A3. Inspect raw or p_wave. Drag color from 0 to 0.5, then release. In Edit change sin(angle * 2) to sin(angle * 3), play A3 again, and inspect the moved harmonic. Undo both changes before another take. Use low notes: arbitrary formulas have no automatic anti-aliasing.
